scope: Incremental hover responsiveness and lifecycle safeguards on main PR #929; targeted verification, no full-suite or live-provider acceptance.

architecture.stack: Existing WXT/Vue/TypeScript; no new dependencies or copied reference-repository code.
architecture.scheduler: One upstream hoverScheduler, with optional availability and owner/session commit guards; same-candidate dwell and request-domain semantics retained.
architecture.candidateResolver: Reuse native hit stack and ancestor guards only within a single synchronous read-only resolution; no cross-call or cross-gesture DOM cache.
architecture.glossaryMemo: One bounded primitive mirror; revalidate every relevant mutable field, order and descriptor on each capture; uncommon or unsafe shapes fall back to the existing revision builder. Each request keeps its own snapshot.
architecture.hostCompatibility: Keep shared candidates, editable/formula barriers, native selection/input/link behavior, default/quick profiles, zero-delay behavior, restore/retranslate and explicit retry.

crossCandidatePerformance.method: Trusted CDP moves alternate two native paragraph owners; synchronous capture-to-bubble plus full-phase CDP metrics including animation-frame work; no upstream translation
crossCandidatePerformance.snapshotPolicy: Entering a different delivered candidate captures a new snapshot; animation-frame coalescing may deliver fewer candidate changes than input events
crossCandidatePerformance.interpretation: Synchronous capture-to-bubble event timing and full-phase CDP ScriptDuration including animation-frame work overlap and cannot be added. Large-minus-empty script duration is glossary-associated workload, not a precise snapshot-function measurement. These are input-work costs, not provider or end-to-end translation latency.

limitations: Browser transport is a deterministic local fixture; actual translation-provider acceptance is unverified.
Firefox and userscript build/verifier success does not establish runtime acceptance on those platforms.
The 135,120-character giant source still has one 51 ms long task during first translation; the cross-candidate performance samples have no long tasks.
Selection/profile arbitration is covered by targeted tests; the browser script does not independently accept every selection-translation path.
Results measure this controlled workload on this machine; no claim of universal end-to-end speed or complete elimination of jank.
